thread:
support-bot: customer message forwarded — tool call failing when payload comes from Windows client. error: "Invalid tool args JSON: Unexpected character '“' at position 14"

jenn: can you paste the exact command they used?

support-bot: pasted from customer (PowerShell paste):
```powershell
curl.exe -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/toolcall -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-***' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d “{"filePath": "C:\Users\Alice\Documents\report.docx", "options": {"ocr": true,},}”
```

jenn: yep — those are smart quotes around the JSON and a trailing comma after "ocr": true, plus Windows backslashes. PowerShell pastes and Word can introduce “curly” quotes which break our JSON parser.

samir: repro'd locally with the same curl string in pwsh. server error log: 
```
error: tool_call_validation_failed
cause: json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Unexpected character '“' (U+201C) at pos 0
payload_snippet: “{"filePath": "C:\\Users\\Alice\\Documents\\report.docx", "options": {"ocr": true,},}”
```

samir: root cause is not escaping + non-ascii smart quotes. parser fails early and we return generic 400. we should improve diagnostics and tolerate common paste issues or at least return a helpful error pointing to illegal char and suggest checking quotes/backslashes.

jenn: temporary workarounds for support to send to customer: 
- re-run in cmd/pwsh but use plain ascii quotes: -d '{"filePath":"C:\Users\Alice\Documents\report.docx","options":{"ocr":true}}'
- or in pwsh use: -d @'{"filePath":"C:\Users\Alice\Documents\report.docx","options":{"ocr":true}}'@ (here-doc style)
- base64 the JSON and use our toolcall base64 field (internal workaround)

jenn: example safe pwsh command:
```powershell
$body = '{"filePath":"C:\Users\Alice\Documents\report.docx","options":{"ocr":true}}'
curl.exe -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/toolcall -H "Authorization: Bearer $env:REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d $body
```

maria: can we escalate this? customer hit this in prod and it blocked an integration. suggest P2 — add actionable error for invalid first character and link to troubleshooting doc. also add a small sanitization step in the SDKs to normalize smart quotes -> straight quotes before sending.

samir: agree. I'll open INC-1234, assign to eng-runtime, label: toolcall-json-escape. quick server-side patch: detect non-ascii quotes and return 400 with message: "Invalid JSON in tool args: detected non-ASCII quotes or unescaped backslashes. Try re-sending with ASCII double quotes (\"\") or escape backslashes (\\)."

jenn: leaving reproduction steps and the pwsh snippet in the ticket. tagging @eng-runtime for rollout.

maria: thanks — replied to customer with the three workaround options and escalation note :thumbsup:

support-bot: closing the slack thread, ticket INC-1234 created (link: https://issues.redwood.ai/INC-1234)
